subject: Clinical Scoring Systems
title: Medical & Surgical Stratification: CURB-65 & Child-Pugh
preview: Apply CURB-65 to pneumonia severity assessment alongside clinical judgement; understand the purpose of Child-Pugh and Apgar scoring.

sections.title: Pneumonia: CURB-65
points: The five components assess new confusion, elevated urea, tachypnea, hypotension and older age; each adds one point.
Use the score together with oxygenation, comorbidities, pregnancy and clinical judgement when deciding place of care.

sections.title: Liver disease and newborn assessment
points: Child-Pugh classes use bilirubin, albumin, INR/prothrombin-time measures, ascites and encephalopathy; it helps describe prognostic severity.
Apgar evaluates appearance, pulse, grimace response, activity and respiration at defined early postnatal time points.

sections.title: Memory aid
points: CURB-65: Confusion, Urea, Respiratory rate, Blood pressure, Age 65 or more.
The score supports clinical judgment, not a rigid discharge rule.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A scoring tool assists but never overrides dangerous clinical findings.
Apgar is not a reason to delay effective newborn ventilation.

quickRevision: CURB-65 summarizes confusion, urea, respiratory rate, blood pressure and age in adults with community-acquired pneumonia.
Child-Pugh describes chronic liver-disease severity using bilirubin, albumin, coagulation, ascites and encephalopathy.
Apgar summarizes neonatal condition after birth; resuscitation decisions are not based on waiting for the Apgar score.

quiz.question: Which disease is commonly assessed with CURB-65?
quiz.explanation: Community-acquired pneumonia. CURB-65: Confusion, Urea, Respiratory rate, Blood pressure, Age 65 or more.
